intended_object: The underlying linear map k^G → X, f ↦ ∑_s f(s)·ρ_X(s⁻¹)v. It is the linear part of the G-equivariant map from the right regular representation to X that sends δ₁ to v (docstring and its use in `ofRightFDRep`).
explanation:
This is a helper in the proof of Tannaka duality for finite groups. It packages only the underlying k-linear map, so that `ofRightFDRep` can bundle it into a morphism in `FDRep k G`. That morphism is then used only to prove `toRightFDRepComp_injective`. A bare linear map to a representation's carrier, with the equivariance proved separately, is an implementation step rather than a standard object in its own right.

The formula is still correct. The right regular action is (t·f)(s) = f(st). Substituting u = st gives φ(t·f) = ∑_s f(st)ρ(s⁻¹)v = ∑_u f(u)ρ(t u⁻¹)v = ρ(t)φ(f), so the map is equivariant. It also sends single 1 1 to v, as the docstring says. Requiring a finite group (`Fintype G`) is needed here, because the formula is a sum over all of G.
